purpose: Gauge-first research decisions for the initial West Virginia route cohort. This is a research artifact, not live route data.

gaugeDecisions.reason: Fresh discharge and stage are available. American Whitewater ties the gauge directly to its Bluestone-Dam-to-Sandstone reach with a 1.35-5.0 foot runnable range, and NPS confirms multiple public access points within that reach. The selected candidate stops at Hellems Beach and therefore does not cross the mandatory Sandstone Falls portage.

Fresh discharge and stage are available. American Whitewater publishes gauge-specific numeric ranges for the Sandstone-McCreery, McCreery-Thurmond, Thurmond-Cunard, and Cunard-Fayette Station reaches. NPS independently confirms the named public access chain and distinguishes the intermediate upper river from the advanced/expert river below Thurmond.

Fresh discharge and stage are available. NPS publishes an exact 4-7 foot safe navigation range on the Pipestem gauge and recognizes the Pipestem-to-Bluestone-State-Park paddling corridor. The current candidate remains operationally blocked until the new tram's private-boat carriage policy is explicit.

candidates.route: Tug Creek River Access to Hellems Beach

putIn.name: Tug Creek River Access
putIn.coordinateSource: American Whitewater access feature; public-access name independently confirmed by NPS

takeOut.name: Hellems Beach River Access
takeOut.coordinateSource: American Whitewater access feature; public-access name independently confirmed by NPS

threshold.scopeNote: The threshold is published for the containing Bluestone-Dam-to-Sandstone reach and uses the same Hinton gauge; the selected subreach is downstream of the gauge and ends before Sandstone Falls.

safety: Brooks Falls is a Class III feature with a consequential keeper hole right of the traditional river-left line.
The NPS characterizes Hinton-to-Thurmond paddling as challenging Class I-III suitable for intermediate whitewater paddlers.
The route intentionally ends well upstream of Sandstone Falls, which NPS/AW treat as a mandatory portage boundary.

camping.note: NPS campgrounds exist elsewhere along the upper New River, but no camping is represented as part of this short route.

candidates.closureCheck: NPS current closure page reviewed 2026-08-25; it did not list Tug Creek or Hellems Beach as closed.
remainingWork: Run coordinate-to-river and official access-registry audits.
Confirm the short route has enough standalone product value versus serving as an access-planner option.

candidates.gaugeRelationship: same-river downstream proxy within published reach

putIn.coordinateSource: American Whitewater access feature; public-access name independently confirmed by NPS

takeOut.coordinateSource: American Whitewater access feature; public-access name independently confirmed by NPS

threshold.scopeNote: AW explicitly identifies Glade Creek to Grandview Sandbar as the popular 4.5-mile trip inside the thresholded containing reach.

safety: Grassy Shoals and Quinnimont are the principal Class III- features on the selected subreach.
At high water, a swim above the Grandview Sandbar takeout can create a missed-ramp risk.
The NPS describes the upper New as a large, powerful river even where rapids are easier.

camping.note: NPS lists designated camping at both Glade Creek and Grandview Sandbar; normal campground rules and first-come availability apply.

remainingWork: Run coordinate-to-river and official access-registry audits.

candidates.route: McCreery River Access to Stone Cliff
candidates.gaugeRelationship: same-river downstream proxy within published reach

putIn.coordinateSource: American Whitewater access feature; public-access name independently confirmed by NPS

takeOut.name: Stone Cliff
takeOut.coordinateSource: American Whitewater access feature; public-access name independently confirmed by NPS

threshold.scopeNote: AW recommends Stone Cliff as the usual takeout within its McCreery-to-Thurmond thresholded reach.

safety: Ledges and Silo are Class III features; Silo has a reported river-right undercut and consequential hydraulics at some levels.
The NPS rates the upper river as appropriate for intermediate whitewater paddlers, not casual flatwater users.
The selected Stone Cliff takeout avoids adding a low-value final pool to Thurmond.

camping.note: NPS lists Stone Cliff among its current New River camping areas.

candidates.closureCheck: NPS current closure page reviewed 2026-08-25; McCreery and Stone Cliff river accesses were not listed as closed.
remainingWork: Run coordinate-to-river and official access-registry audits.
Calibrate product messaging so a broad runnable range does not imply uniformly beginner-friendly hydraulics.

candidates.blocker: Published distance conflict and safety-framing conflict must be resolved before implementation.
candidates.difficulty: Class I-III in AW; below-Thurmond advanced/expert framing in NPS

putIn.name: Thurmond
putIn.coordinateSource: American Whitewater access feature; NPS confirms the public Thurmond/Dunglen access family

takeOut.name: Cunard
takeOut.coordinateSource: American Whitewater access feature; public-access name independently confirmed by NPS

safety: Surprise is a Class III rapid with a large hole at some flows.
NPS says the New River downstream from Thurmond is suitable only for advanced and expert paddlers.
Cunard Road is steep and partly gravel; it is currently one lane in places and closes seasonally November through March.

camping.note: NPS lists several nearby New River camps, but no camping is represented as part of this selected reach.

candidates.closureCheck: NPS reports Cunard Road open as of 2026-08-06, with one-lane delays through October and a planned November-March closure.
candidates.nextAction: Resolve mileage from an official route line or generated river geometry, then preserve NPS advanced/expert posture even if AW retains a lower reach rating.

safety: NPS restricts the below-Thurmond river to advanced and expert paddlers and warns of powerful currents, hydraulics, boulders, and undercut rocks.
The reach has a substantial recorded accident history and must remain hidden from default recreational discovery.
Cunard Road is steep, partly gravel, one lane during current work, and seasonally closed November-March.

camping.note: Brooklyn and other NPS camps can support a trip but are not represented as on-route or endpoint camping.

candidates.closureCheck: NPS reports Cunard Road open as of 2026-08-06, with one-lane delays through October. Fayette Station was not listed as closed.

Review whether the published AW upper range needs a more conservative Paddle Today danger cutoff.

candidates.route: Pipestem Resort State Park to Bluestone State Park
candidates.blocker: Current official tram material confirms seasonal river access but does not explicitly confirm private kayak/canoe carriage on the replacement gondola.
candidates.difficulty: Class I-II below the tram; remote scenic river

putIn.name: Pipestem Resort State Park / Mountain Creek Lodge tram river access
putIn.coordinateSource: American Whitewater access feature; NPS and WV State Parks independently confirm tram connection to the Bluestone River

takeOut.name: Bluestone State Park / Turnpike Trail river access
takeOut.coordinateSource: American Whitewater access feature; NPS independently confirms Bluestone State Park as the downstream corridor endpoint

threshold.scopeNote: Use the narrower official NPS 4-7 foot safe-navigation range rather than AW's broader 4-10 foot runnable range.

safety: The river is remote and frequently too low, especially in summer.
Tram operation is seasonal and weather-dependent, so same-day access confirmation is mandatory.
The lower miles transition toward Bluestone Lake backwater and require sustained flatwater paddling.
Camping and fires are prohibited within Bluestone National Scenic River.

camping.note: NPS prohibits camping in the scenic-river unit but identifies campground/lodging options at Pipestem Resort and Bluestone State Parks.

candidates.closureCheck: WV State Parks advertises the new tram as operating May-October weather permitting; no explicit boat-cargo policy was found in the current official page.
candidates.nextAction: Obtain current written confirmation that private paddlecraft can be carried on the tram, including size, fee, reservation, operating-day, and shutdown rules. If not, research Lilly or another official road-access endpoint instead.
